01 / THE CACHE

Give the receiver
something to keep.

Each group starts with the complete scene. After that, the selected Gaussians get fresh records; everything else stays at its first-frame value. Scrub back to the start of a group: the two views match again.

N + M(K − 1)   vs   NK

N is the full scene, M the update count and K the group length. This comparison assumes equal-size records. It omits headers, indices, residual coding and compression. It is not a bitrate estimate.

02 / THE SURPRISE

Still in space.
Changing in time.

The left panel doesn’t move. Its color does. Switch to “Position only” and those changes can be missed. Raise the update budget, or let color participate in the ranking, to see which information gets through.

A fixed position ≠ a fixed appearance

Longer groups offer more reuse but can make stale values more visible. In this toy, the ranking itself also changes with group length, so the error need not increase monotonically.

03 / THE NEW CONNECTION

Spend updates
where they matter.

ResStreamGS (15 Oct 2026) separates reusable Gaussian information from time-varying updates. Its six-sequence evaluation supports a scoped result against a controlled baseline, rather than a universal compression ranking.

The lab makes the reuse trade-off visible. It does not implement the paper’s learned probe, residual representation, training or codec. Read the method ↗

What you’re looking at

466 hand-designed 3D Gaussians, analytic motion and changing colors, perspective covariance projection and center-depth alpha sorting. The camera is fixed during each cycle. The toy selects whole Gaussian records using future synthetic trajectories sampled across each group; it does not learn which attributes are stable. Pixel RMSE compares two analytic 120 × 80 rasterizations on a 0–1 RGB scale; the larger display uses a visually similar Gaussian falloff. A lower record count is not measured network traffic or a compression ratio in bytes. At every group boundary the cache resets, which can create visible jumps. No generated footage, trained model, codec or paper benchmark runs here.
